report.source_text: The role of surgery was discussed with the patient and, given the presumptive diagnosis of ependymoma, complete resection of the lesion was planned. A L1/2 laminectomy was subsequently undertaken with midline dural opening. The tumor was identified within the conus and seen tracking down the filum terminale. Separate to the conus, tumor was found encasing the right side of the cauda equina and, when dissected apart, the affected nerve roots contained intraneural tumor. No clear tumor–conus interface was seen. Therefore, the conus component was debulked in a piecemeal fashion and sent with biopsies of the cauda equina component for histopathological analysis.

Surgical exploration via L1/2 laminectomy identified tumor within the conus tracking down the filum terminale, and separate tumor encasing the right cauda equina with intraneural involvement of affected nerve roots. report.source_text: Histology demonstrated features of classic HL involving spinal cord parenchyma and peripheral nerve fascicles. The tumor tissue was composed of scattered Hodgkin cells, Reed–Sternberg cells and lacunar cells surrounded by a mix of small lymphocytes, histiocytes, eosinophils and occasional neutrophils (Figure 2). No prominent fibrous bands were present and, therefore, the mixed cellularity subtype was favored. On immunohistochemistry, the tumor cells showed membrane staining for CD30.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (mixed cellularity subtype) involving spinal cord parenchyma and peripheral nerve fascicles
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old female presented with a 2-month history of lower back pain and 4-week history of right L5-S1 radiculopathy with perianal paresthesia, progressing to anal and urinary sphincter dysfunction with incomplete bowel emptying and occasional urinary incontinence. Physical examination revealed preserved motor function, loss of sensation in S3-5 dermatomes, and preserved reflexes. MRI lumbosacral spine identified a lobulated homogeneously enhancing exophytic lesion involving the conus medullaris and filum terminale (13 × 14 × 22 mm at L1/2 level) with cord edema extending to T11, plus a small 5 mm lesion in the cauda equina at L5/S1. Surgical exploration via L1/2 laminectomy revealed tumor within the conus tracking down the filum terminale and separate tumor encasing the right cauda equina with intraneural involvement of affected nerve roots. Histopathology of surgical specimens confirmed classic Hodgkin lymphoma (mixed cellularity subtype) with Hodgkin cells, Reed-Sternberg cells, and lacunar cells surrounded by mixed inflammatory infiltrate. Immunohistochemistry showed CD30 positive, weak CD20/PAX5 positive, MUM1 positive, EBER positive, and CD45 negative, excluding alternative lymphoma subtypes. PET/CT staging showed no further CNS involvement or systemic disease. Following treatment (including radiotherapy), at 10 months postoperatively the patient was well with no motor deficit and normal bowel and bladder function, with complete resolution of enhancement on MRI at both L1/2 and L5/S1 levels and no further disease on follow-up cranio-spinal imaging.
